summary.text: 七 is the numeral character for “seven.” Early crossed forms are documented writing the numeral, while a competing analysis treats the graph as an earlier sign for “cut” that was later borrowed for seven; the original referent remains disputed.

formation.text: The formation is disputed. One analysis treats the crossed graph as a pictograph or indicative sign for cutting across a line, later borrowed to write the numeral; another account documents the crossed graph as the numeral from oracle-bone writing onward. Neither the original referent nor the proposed borrowing sequence is established.

history.text: The selected oracle-script-style image shows crossed horizontal and vertical strokes; the seal-style redraw bends the lower vertical stroke. These are modern redrawings of script forms, not photographs of artifacts. A paleographic study reports the crossing form from oracle-bone writing through early Western Han clerical forms and says the lower stroke’s rightward bend became established after the Eastern Han, possibly to distinguish 七 from 十. Another account explains the seal form’s bend in this way; the graphic sequence is reported, but the explanation is not uniform.

The cut-origin account says the graph was borrowed for the numeral and that 刀 was added to form 切. Other evidence records numeral use from oracle-bone writing onward, so this proposed character-to-character history remains disputed; the dossier does not establish a matched historical pronunciation for 七 and 切.
The Shuowen Jiezi interprets the graph through a cosmological account of yang and yin. This is a historical explanation of the graph, not independent evidence for its original referent.

uncertainties.text: The earliest graphic referent and spoken name are not independently established here. The cut interpretation and its proposed borrowing sequence remain disputed, and the proposed sound connection with 切 is not verified by a matched reconstruction pair.

The transmitted Shijing text contains numeral uses, but its physical witness and composition date are not established by the supplied evidence; it therefore does not settle the earliest surviving written attestation.

senses.period: Oracle-bone writing onward, as reported by a paleographic study
senses.text: A paleographic study reports 七 used for the numeral in oracle-bone writing and cites an oracle-bone example. This establishes an early numeral use in the study’s account, without resolving whether an earlier cut-related use preceded it.

senses.gloss: seven (Japanese readings なな and しち)
senses.period: Manyōshū example dated to the 8th century; later attestations also recorded
senses.text: Japanese lexical evidence records なな for “seven” in an 8th-century Manyōshū example and a しち example from 1477. These attestations concern Japanese readings and use, not the origin of the Chinese graph.
A specialized Japanese dictionary sense “gambler” is recorded with an example dated 1744; the evidence does not explain its development from “seven.”

limitations.text: The dossier supports early numeral use but does not settle whether that was the graph’s original meaning. It does not establish a semantic path from “seven” to the later Japanese sense “gambler.”

overview.text: 七 is the character for “seven.” Crossed forms are documented as numeral writing from oracle-bone evidence onward, though one disputed account proposes that the graph first represented cutting and was later borrowed for the number.
